questions.answer: Degrees: $A = 4$ (edges to $B$, $C$, $D$ and the curved edge to $D$), $B = 2$, $C = 3$, $D = 3$. Two vertices ($C$ and $D$) have odd degree. **(B)**

questions.question: Which of the following could be the equation of the function drawn in the diagram?
questions.answer: The line slopes down (negative gradient) and crosses the $y$-axis above the origin (positive $y$-intercept): $y = -3x + 1$. **(C)**

questions.question: An electrician charges a call-out fee of \$150 as well as \$4 per minute while working. Which equation expresses the amount the electrician charges (\$$E$) as a function of time ($t$ hours)?
questions.answer: \$4 per minute is $4 \times 60 = \$240$ per hour, so $E = 150 + 240t$. **(D)**

questions.question: The diagram shows a triangle with side lengths 10 m, 12 m and 13 m. The angle $\theta$ is opposite the 13 m side. What is the value of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree?
questions.answer: $$\cos\theta = \frac{10^2 + 12^2 - 13^2}{2 \times 10 \times 12} = \frac{75}{240} \implies \theta \approx 72^\circ. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

questions.question: Which expression can be used to convert a speed of 5 metres per minute to a speed in centimetres per second?
questions.answer: 5 m/min $= 5 \times 100$ cm/min $= 5 \times 100 \div 60$ cm/s. **(A)**

questions.question: How many square centimetres are in 4 square metres?

A solid is made up of a square pyramid stacked on a cube, as in the diagram. The cube has side 8 cm and the total height of the solid is 21 cm. What is its volume, correct to the nearest cubic centimetre?
questions.answer:
Pyramid height $= 21 - 8 = 13$ cm.
$$V = 8^3 + \frac13 \times 8^2 \times 13 = 512 + 277.33 \approx 789.3 \approx 790\ \text{cm}^3. \quad \textbf{(B)}$$

questions.question: The marks in a test were normally distributed. The mean mark was 65 and the standard deviation was 12. What was the percentage of marks between 53 and 89?
questions.answer: 53 has $z = -1$ and 89 has $z = 2$. By the empirical rule: $34\% + 47.5\% = 81.5\%$. **(C)**

| First Class | \$188 |

Frankie is travelling to Melbourne for a friend's wedding on the long weekend in October. She plans to take a Sleeper on the downwards journey and an Economy seat on the return. There is no discount for return tickets. What is the price of the entire trip before GST?
questions.answer: Total including GST $= 220 + 133 = \$353$. Before GST: $353 \div 1.1 = \$320.91$. **(B)**

questions.question: A loaded six-sided die is biased so that it lands on 3 twice as often as it lands on any other number. What is the probability that, when it is rolled, it lands on a number other than 3?
questions.answer: Think of 7 equally likely 'slots': two for 3 and one each for 1, 2, 4, 5, 6. So $P(\text{not } 3) = \dfrac57$. **(D)**

questions.question: The maximum speed of a train going up a hill varies inversely with the square of its weight. What is the effect on the maximum speed of the train if the weight of the train is halved?
questions.answer: $S = \dfrac{k}{w^2}$. Halving $w$: $S = \dfrac{k}{(w/2)^2} = \dfrac{4k}{w^2}$, so the speed is multiplied by 4. **(D)**

questions.question: Five years ago a refrigerator was valued at \$2568. Its value has depreciated by 18% each year, based on the declining-balance method. Find its salvage value today, correct to the nearest dollar.

Seth is a registered nurse and works a 40 hour week at an ordinary rate of \$37.12 per hour.

Last week he worked his normal 40 hours and an extra 9 hours of overtime at time-and-a-half. Calculate his total pay for the week.

Seth is a registered nurse and works a 40 hour week at an ordinary rate of \$37.12 per hour.

He has a holiday planned in August and will receive four weeks' wages plus 17.5% holiday loading. Calculate his total holiday pay.
questions.answer: Four weeks' wages: $40 \times 37.12 \times 4 = \$5939.20$. With 17.5% loading: $5939.20 \times 1.175 = \$6978.56$.

questions.question: The recent World Cup football game between Australia and Paraguay was broadcast live at 12 pm on Friday 26 June in Sydney (UTC+10). Paolo watched the game live in Paraguay (UTC−3). What time did the game start in Paraguay and what day was it?
questions.answer: Paraguay is $10 + 3 = 13$ hours behind Sydney. $12\text{ pm} - 13\text{ h} = 11\text{ pm}$ the previous day: **11 pm on Thursday 25 June**.

questions.question: The diagram shows points $O$ and $B$, with $B$ south-east of $O$ and $\angle$ (south direction from $O$, $OB$) $= 65^\circ$. What is the bearing of $O$ from $B$?
questions.answer: The bearing of $B$ from $O$ is $180^\circ - 65^\circ = 115^\circ$. The reverse bearing is $115^\circ + 180^\circ = 295^\circ$T (or N$65^\circ$W).

questions.question: A map has a scale of 1 : 200 000. Two lighthouses are 3 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the two lighthouses? Give your answer in kilometres.
Carlo drove 480 km in 6 hours and 10 minutes. If he averaged 75 km/h for the first 200 km, how long did it take him to travel the remainder of his trip?
questions.answer: First 200 km: $\dfrac{200}{75} = 2\frac23$ h $= 2$ h 40 min. Remainder: $6\text{ h }10\text{ min} - 2\text{ h }40\text{ min} = $ **3 h 30 min**.

questions.question:
Electricity is charged at 32.56 cents per kWh. A household uses the following appliances:
- An 880 W oven for 2 hours, five times a week
- A 3.25 kW washing machine, for 3 hours, once per day
- A 300 W lamp running 12 hours a day.

Calculate the total electricity cost to run all three appliances for a full 7-day week, if the lamp uses 0.2 W when on standby. Both the oven and the washing machine use no power when on standby.
questions.answer:
- Oven: $0.88 \times 2 \times 5 = 8.8$ kWh
- Washing machine: $3.25 \times 3 \times 7 = 68.25$ kWh
- Lamp: on $0.3 \times 12 \times 7 = 25.2$ kWh; standby $0.0002 \times 12 \times 7 = 0.0168$ kWh

Total $= 102.2668$ kWh. Cost $= 102.2668 \times 0.3256 \approx \$33.30$.

questions.question:
A network of power poles and the distances between them in metres is shown. The edges are $AB = 20$, $BC = 25$, $AC = 40$, $AF = 20$, $CF = 22$, $AG = 20$, $FG = 25$, $FE = 25$, $CD = 22$, $CE = 35$, $DE = 15$ and $GE = 30$.

Find the length of the shortest path from pole $B$ to pole $E$.
questions.answer: $B \to C \to E = 25 + 35 = 60$ m (compare $B \to C \to D \to E = 62$ m and $B \to A \to F \to E = 65$ m). Shortest: **60 m**.

questions.question:
A network of power poles and the distances between them in metres is shown. The edges are $AB = 20$, $BC = 25$, $AC = 40$, $AF = 20$, $CF = 22$, $AG = 20$, $FG = 25$, $FE = 25$, $CD = 22$, $CE = 35$, $DE = 15$ and $GE = 30$.

A spanning tree of the network is shown below, with edges $AB = 20$, $BC = 25$, $CD = 22$, $AG = 20$, $FG = 25$ and $GE = 30$. Is this a minimum spanning tree? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
Length of the given tree: $20 + 25 + 22 + 20 + 25 + 30 = 142$ m.

A minimum spanning tree (e.g. by Kruskal's algorithm) uses $DE = 15$, $AB = 20$, $AF = 20$, $AG = 20$, $CF = 22$, $CD = 22$, with length $15 + 20 + 20 + 20 + 22 + 22 = 119$ m.

Since $142 > 119$, the given tree is **not** a minimum spanning tree.

questions.question: A rowing coach claimed that as time spent training on the water decreases, the time to complete a 1000 m time trial on the rowing machine in the gym increases. When she completed some research, she found the correlation coefficient, $r$, to be approximately $-0.84$. What does this value of $r$ indicate and does this value of $r$ support her claim?
questions.answer: $r \approx -0.84$ indicates a **strong negative** linear association: less time training on the water goes with longer time-trial times. This supports her claim (though correlation alone does not prove that one causes the other).

The following formula can be used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for males.
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
$N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms and $H$ is the number of hours drinking.

Gregor weighs 80 kg. His BAC was zero when he began drinking alcohol. At 10 pm, after consuming 6 standard drinks, his BAC was 0.075. Using the formula above, estimate the time at which Gregor began drinking alcohol. Give your answer correct to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$0.075 = \frac{10 \times 6 - 7.5H}{6.8 \times 80} \implies 40.8 = 60 - 7.5H \implies H = 2.56 \text{ h}.$$
$2.56$ h $= 2$ h $33.6$ min $\approx 2$ h 34 min. He began drinking at about $10\text{ pm} - 2\text{ h }34\text{ min} = $ **7:26 pm**.

questions.question: Max and Thomas are playing a game. Thomas is the stronger player and the probability of him winning the game is $\dfrac79$. The boys play two games in a row. What is the probability that both boys win a game?
questions.answer:
Each boy wins one game: Thomas then Max, or Max then Thomas.
$$P = \frac79 \times \frac29 + \frac29 \times \frac79 = \frac{28}{81}.$$

Find the maximum height reached by the ball.
questions.answer: The vertex is at $t = 1$: $h = -5 + 10 + 40 = 45$ m.

questions.question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a balcony and its height $h$ metres above the ground over time $t$ seconds is modelled using the equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$. The graph of $h$ against $t$ is shown.

How long does it take for the ball to return to the height of the balcony and how far has it travelled vertically then?
questions.answer: Balcony height is 40 m: $-5t^2 + 10t = 0 \implies t = 0$ or $t = 2$. It returns after **2 seconds**, having gone up 5 m (to 45 m) and down 5 m: **10 m** travelled.

questions.question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a balcony and its height $h$ metres above the ground over time $t$ seconds is modelled using the equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$. The graph of $h$ against $t$ is shown.

The equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$ only models the flight of the ball for some values of $t$. Explain which values are invalid and why.
questions.answer:
- $t < 0$: time cannot be negative (before the ball is thrown).
- $t > 4$: the ball hits the ground at $t = 4$ ($h = 0$); after that the model gives negative heights, i.e. below the ground, which is impossible.

The model is only valid for $0 \le t \le 4$.

questions.answer: Read across from $P = 1000$: $t \approx 2.6$ minutes (exactly $\frac{\ln 2}{\ln 1.3} \approx 2.64$).

questions.question:
A population $P$ is to be modelled using the function $P = 500(1.3)^t$, where $t$ is the time in minutes since the start of the population growth.

Predict when the population will be fifty times its initial value. Give your answer correct to the nearest minute.
questions.answer: We need $P = 50 \times 500 = 25\,000$. Testing: $t = 14$ gives $500(1.3)^{14} \approx 19\,687$; $t = 15$ gives $500(1.3)^{15} \approx 25\,593$. So after about **15 minutes**.

questions.question:
A small business operator pays her staff the following wages per week, depending on their experience:

\$210, \$350, \$410, \$510, \$580, \$610, \$985

Is the highest wage an outlier? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
Median \$510; $Q_1 = \$350$, $Q_3 = \$610$, so $\text{IQR} = 260$.

Upper fence $= Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 610 + 390 = \$1000$. Since $985 < 1000$, the highest wage is **not** an outlier.

questions.question:
A small business operator pays her staff the following wages per week, depending on their experience:

\$210, \$350, \$410, \$510, \$580, \$610, \$985

If each employee receives a pay increase of \$45, which of the following summary statistics will change: the range, mean, median and/or standard deviation?
questions.answer: Adding the same amount to every value shifts the data but not their spread: the **mean and median** increase by \$45; the range and standard deviation do not change.

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

Farmer Tran wants to fence around the area $ABOD$. Find the cost of this project if each metre of fencing costs \$22.
questions.answer:
$\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 310^\circ + 21^\circ = 71^\circ$ and $\angle AOD = 310^\circ - 256^\circ = 54^\circ$.
$$AB^2 = 85^2 + 64^2 - 2(85)(64)\cos 71^\circ \implies AB \approx 88.20 \text{ m}$$
$$AD^2 = 85^2 + 70^2 - 2(85)(70)\cos 54^\circ \implies AD \approx 71.63 \text{ m}$$
Perimeter of $ABOD = 88.20 + 64 + 70 + 71.63 \approx 293.82$ m. Cost $\approx 293.82 \times 22 = \$6464.13$.

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

The surveyor finds that the area of triangle $BOC$ is $1664\ \text{m}^2$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $O$.
questions.answer:
$\frac12 \times 64 \times 52 \times \sin\angle BOC = 1664 \implies \sin\angle BOC = 1 \implies \angle BOC = 90^\circ$.

Bearing of $C$ from $O$ $= 21^\circ + 90^\circ = 111^\circ$T.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

By forward scanning, find the earliest start time of activity $K$.
questions.answer:
ESTs: $C$: 3; $D$, $E$: $\max(6, 3 + 2) = 6$; $J$: $6 + 5 = 11$; $F$: 3.

$K$ starts after $F$ (finishes at 8) and $J$ (finishes at 14): **EST of $K$ = 14 weeks**.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

Identify any critical paths and find how many of the 13 activities have zero float time.
questions.answer:
Forward scan: $G$ starts at 9, $H$/$I$/$J$ at 11, $L$ at $\max(9 + 4, 11 + 2) = 13$, $M$ at $\max(13 + 5, 11 + 2) = 18$; finish $= \max(18 + 1, 14 + 3) = 19$ weeks.

Critical paths (length 19): **$A$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$** and **$A$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$**.

Activities with zero float: $A, D, E, G, H, L, M$ — **7 activities**.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

The project currently takes 19 weeks. The contractor proposes a reduction in completion time for activities $A$, $E$, $F$ and $L$, at an additional cost. The table below summarises these costs. Each activity can only be reduced by a maximum of three weeks.

| Activity | Weekly cost (\$) |
|---|---|
| $A$ | 130 000 |
| $E$ | 110 000 |
| $F$ | 120 000 |
| $L$ | 100 000 |

If the overall completion time for the project can be reduced to 15 weeks, find the minimum cost of this change. Your answer should explain clearly why the minimum cost is achieved.
questions.answer:
Every path must end up at most 15 weeks. Let $a$, $e$, $l$ be the reductions of $A$, $E$, $L$ ($F$ is on no long path, so reducing it does not help).

| Path | Length | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| $A$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + l \ge 4$ |
| $A$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + e + l \ge 4$ |
| $B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $l \ge 3$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $e + l \ge 3$ |
| $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 17 | $a + e \ge 2$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 16 | $e \ge 1$ |

$B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ forces $l = 3$ (the maximum), so $a + l \ge 4$ forces $a \ge 1$; $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ forces $e \ge 1$. Taking $a = 1$, $e = 1$, $l = 3$ meets every condition:
$$\text{Minimum cost} = 130\,000 + 110\,000 + 3 \times 100\,000 = \$540\,000.$$

(The paper's sample answer gives \$430 000 by reducing only $A$ and $L$, but that leaves $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks and $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks, so the project would still take 16 weeks.)
